newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen up on OTC, San Onofre news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen up on OTC, San Onofre news.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open sharply higher Thursday, taking a cue from a jump in over-the-counter (OTC) prices and news that the restart of San Onofre 3 nuclear unit was delayed.
July Palo Verde (PV) futures, in OTC activity, were quoted at $34.00-34.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Wednesday's settlement at $32.66 after exchanges as high as $36.50.
July OTC California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $21.50-22.50 versus yesterday's close at $20.10.
Restart of the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 unit in southern California was delayed to July 10 July from late June to repair a coupling problem, the operator Southern California Edison Co said today.

Although most six to 10 day forecasts still showed normal to slightly above normal readings in the West, the National Weather Service revised its earlier outlook calling for warmer than normal temperatures across the region.
July PV in three days rose almost $5.00 or 18 percent, approaching its life-of-contract high of $33.75 while July COB gained $2.30 or 12.9 percent, well below its contract high of $24.75.
A steady stream of news about short-term plant outages and forecasts of persistent heat in the interior section of the Southwest remained the driving force behind the complex's rise this week.
Technically, analysts said the complex continued to look bullish with PV holding its long-term trendlines.
In the West, Salt River Project (SRP) said its 750 MW unit 3 at its Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Arizona, tripped off line early Tuesday, but was boosting power the same day.
All three Navajo units had been operating at half load over the past few days due to mild weather and weak demand, SRP said.

Pacific Gas & Electric Co said its Moss Landing natural gas-fired plant in Monterey, Calif., tripped off line late Monday. One of the two 750 MW unit was expected to resume operation yesterday afternoon and the other today.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico tripped off line Wednesday morning due to a tube rupture, with no information available on a restart.
A new outage was seen at the 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired plant in Montana. That unit was expected to return to service early Thursday.

The complex was also bolstered by a Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) committee introduction of a proposal to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system from July 1-30 to 6,300 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
The plan still requires the approval of the WSCC board.
